Dingemans' own Special B® MD is specified at 270-350 EBC and 115.00 Lovibond, which agrees with Castle's 98.1-120.6 to within the width of either range. Two maltsters independently put this malt near 110 Lovibond; the stored 180 was not close to either. The maltster backs extract and colour and nothing else on this record. The ppg, colour and diastatic power on this record are unsourced, and the citation was a homepage that no longer has anything behind it. rahrmalting.com answers every path with a 114-byte document whose only content is a script redirecting to /lander, and /lander carries no text at all. An earlier version of this note said the Internet Archive had declined, and that was wrong — worth correcting, because it would stop the next person looking. The Archive is almost certainly holding snapshots of the old site. What is true is narrower and is about this project's environment, not about the Archive: archive.org itself is reachable from here and is cited elsewhere in this catalogue, but web.archive.org is not reachable at all — curl gets no connection, and the harness fetcher refuses the host outright — while archive.org's wayback availability API returns 429 across hours. Anyone with a browser should go and look; the snapshots are very likely there and this is a limitation of the machine that built this record.

The distributor route was tried too and is a dead end for specifications. Rahr's own distribution arm, RahrBSG, is live at rahrbsg.com and rahrbsg.ca and already supplies this catalogue with hop data sheets, but its malt pages are a JavaScript storefront: the supplier page for Rahr Malting Co. carries no analysis and no PDF, and the Canadian product sitemap lists Simpsons and Muntons malts without a single Rahr-branded one. No distributor's copy of a maltster's figures was substituted in place of the maltster's.

fermentables.name: Crystal Malt 77°L
fermentables.description: Classic English medium-dark crystal; rich toffee and dried fruit for bitters and old ales.
fermentables.attribution: Crisp Malt's published typical analysis for Crystal 77L Malt. Extract is 71.5% dry basis in their typical analysis, and this project's scale is 46 x extract, so ppg is 32.9, against a stored 34. Colour is published as 94-110 Lovibond (225-265 EBC by IoB, 247-291 EBC by the EBC method), so the midpoint is 102.0, against a stored 77. Moisture is given as 3.5% max.
fermentables.sourceNote: The malt's own name disagrees with its maker's analysis and the analysis wins. Crisp sell this as Crystal 77L, and the stored colour was that 77; their typical analysis says 94-110 Lovibond. Their table is internally consistent - the Lovibond column is a correct conversion of the EBC column beside it, 247-291 EBC being 94-110 Lovibond - and the same offset appears on Crystal Extra Dark 120L, specified at 158-181 Lovibond. Crystal Light 45L (38-46) and Crystal 60L (61-69) do match their names, so this is not a systematic error in Crisp's tables; the darker two appear to be named to US market convention rather than to their own analysis. Brew to 102, not 77. The maltster backs extract and colour and nothing else on this record. The maximum batch percentage is this project's own guidance, and where a diastatic power is stored it is not from this document.
